note: CODE DERIVATION: the IRW codes WHO1..WHO5 ARE the column names of the study's own S2 data file -- data/hui_2024_gbfs_battery.py melts value_vars=[f'WHO{i}' for i in 1..6] by name, so there is no positional or renaming step. That file carries NO variable or value labels at any level (44 bare codes in the header row), so this is NOT data_labels; the only tie between code and wording is the trailing digit against the WHO-5's fixed canonical item numbering, hence mapping_basis=reconstructed. LANGUAGE: administered in Chinese (paper: 'the Chinese version of WHO-5 [36]'), and the administered Chinese wording is NOT recoverable in scope. Files checked and what they contain: S1 File is the Chinese GBFS questionnaire only (no WHO-5 items); S2 File is the data .xls with bare column codes and no labels; and the study's own cited source for its Chinese WHO-5, Fung et al. (2022) Front Public Health, contains ZERO CJK characters in its full text (checked on the Europe PMC fullTextXML) -- it prints its five items in English only. So this is the documented fallback: English in the base fields, _translated columns empty, language=Chinese, text_source=translated_substitute, translation_source=official_instrument_english. TEXT: item_text, instructions and option_text are the official WHO-5 English form transcribed verbatim from Ganotice et al. (2025) Appendix A (CC BY), including the anchor-to-number grid (All of the time 5, Most of the time 4, More than half of the time 3, Less than half of the time 2, Some of the time 1, At no time 0). ONE DEVIATION TO NAME: that reproduction's worked example ends 'select number three', which is its online-survey rendering of the printed form's 'tick the box'; it is transcribed as printed rather than rewritten. Items carry no trailing full stop, again as printed there (Fung et al.'s Table 2 prints the same five sentences with stops). RESP: 0..5 ascending well-being, stated by the paper ('from 0 (at no time) to 5 (all the time)') and matching the official form's grid; the build does no recoding, only pd.to_numeric, so the items are stored RAW. MAPPING CHECKED (see verify_hui_2024_who5.R, VERDICT: PASS): two independent predictions. (A) Direction and block identity, decisive: on the 302 complete cases the WHO1..WHO5 block reproduces the paper's own published statistics exactly -- Cronbach's alpha 0.9131 against the printed 0.913, and r(GBFS total, WHO-5 total) = +0.3543 against the printed +0.354; reversing the anchors gives -0.3543, so the 0='At no time' direction is pinned rather than assumed. (B) Per-item profile against Iversen et al. (2025) Table 2 (independent nationwide sample, N~2296): item means on the 0-100 scale rank-correlate 0.90 (published 36.23/36.11/30.86/28.98/34.95 for items 1-5 vs observed 65.15/62.18/60.73/57.23/60.46), WHO4 is the lowest-mean item here as item 4 is there, WHO4 also carries the highest floor (3.96% at 0, against 0.33-1.32% for the other four; published floors 35.0% vs 14.2-28.2%), and WHO1 is the highest-mean item as item 1 is there. This does NOT separate every item from every other -- WHO3 and WHO5 differ by 0.27 points on the 0-100 scale (and the published sample orders them the other way round), and WHO1/WHO2 by 2.97 -- so the verification status is PARTIAL, not VERIFIED. STEP 3B: no instrument mismatch. The live block is 5 items on resp 0-5 with an internal consistency that reproduces the paper's WHO-5 alpha to 4 decimals; the GBFS (b1..b28, resp 1-5) and PSS-10 (pss1..pss10, resp 0-4) blocks in the same file are the sibling tables hui_2024_gbfs and hui_2024_pss10 and were not touched. RIGHTS: no restriction found and none quotable. The WHO-5's rights holder (Psychiatric Research Unit, Mental Health Centre North Zealand) states on its own site that 'The purpose of this homepage is to make the WHO (Five) Well-being Index (WHO-Five, WHO-5, or WBI) in different language versions available to all interested parties' -- no fee, no no-redistribution clause, no non-commercial term. The live site is bot-walled (JavaScript challenge), so this was read from the Internet Archive snapshot of 2026-04-11; absence of a retrievable clause is not absence of a clause, but per the 2026-09-04 quote test silence is permission, so the table ships. The wording actually copied came from a CC BY 4.0 Annals of Medicine article. RETRY TEST: NO -- a determinate verdict was reached and the table shipped.
public_note: The WHO-5 was administered to these Chinese college students in Chinese, but no Chinese wording is published in the paper, in either of its supporting files, or in the paper the authors cite as the source of their Chinese version, so the item text shown here is the official English WHO-5 form rather than what respondents read. The item-to-code mapping rests on the instrument's canonical numbering: it is corroborated by the response data (WHO4 is the lowest-scoring item with the highest floor, matching item 4 'I woke up feeling fresh and rested' in published WHO-5 samples, and the scale direction reproduces the paper's own r = +0.354 with the GBFS), but items 3 and 5 are too close in this sample to be told apart that way

note: Level-1 source. The figshare deposit's own workbook (sheet 'Leyenda') prints the Spanish wording of all 40 ASQ items keyed to the codes 'ASQ-1'..'ASQ-40', which are the same codes the 'Data set' sheet uses for the item columns ('ASQ-1 C', 'ASQ-2 C', ...). data/iandolo_2021_asq.py does a number-preserving rename ASQ-(\d+) -> ASQ_\1 over exactly those 40 columns and melts them unchanged, so the IRW item code carries the source column's own number: derivation pattern 2, no positional assignment, mapping exempt from Step 5b. item_text is the Leyenda text verbatim (trailing spaces stripped; the source's own accent/typo inconsistencies -- 'mas', 'dificil', 'deberias', 'facil' -- left as found). The column headers additionally carry the ASQ subscale code (C/DC/RS/NA/PR) and reproduce Feeney, Noller & Hanrahan's (1994) canonical assignment exactly (C 1,2,3,19,31,33,37,38; DC 4,5,16,17,20,21,23,25,26,34; RS 6,7,8,9,10,14,36; NA 11,12,13,15,24,27,35; PR 18,22,28,29,30,32,39,40), matching the paper's Table 2. item_text_translated is Feeney et al.'s original English for the same numbered items, retrieved from psytests.org/ipl/asqen-bl.html (a reproduction of the 1994 instrument, cached under .cache/iandolo_2021_asq/); all 40 correspond one-to-one in meaning with the Spanish. option_text_translated at resp 1 and 6 is the paper's own description of the scale, quoted verbatim: 'a Likert scale of 6 points, ranging from (1) "Strongly disagree" to (6) "totally agree"'; the intermediate anchors are not labelled by the study, so resp 2-5 are left blank rather than padded. option_text (base) is blank throughout because neither the deposit nor the paper publishes the Spanish, Italian or Japanese anchor wording; instructions likewise are not published in either. DIRECTION CHECKED, and a defect found: summing the item columns per the paper's factor definitions reproduces Table 3's published subscale M/SD exactly, but only under a per-subsample scoring rule. F3/F4/F5 (22 items, no reverse items) reproduce in all three groups regardless (e.g. Spain F4 25.00/6.04 vs 25.00/6.07 published; Japan F5 21.77/4.98 vs 21.77/4.98). F1 and F2 contain the reverse-keyed items 33 and 20,21: Spain reproduces ONLY after reversing them (F1 34.78/5.50 vs 34.74/5.41; F2 37.48/8.55 vs 37.48/8.56 -- as stored it is 33.28 and 35.01), while Italy and Japan reproduce ONLY as stored (Italy F1 30.22/5.76 and F2 38.05/7.27, both exact to 2dp; reversed they read 30.12 and 33.69). Per-respondent the stored 'ASQ-Conf'/'ASQ-Mal.Cia' totals match the reversed sum for 129/139 and 130/139 of the Spanish cases and the as-stored sum for 85/85 and 85/85 Italian and 124/130 and 124/130 Japanese cases. r(ASQ_16, ASQ_20) is -0.687 in Spain and +0.577/+0.397 in Italy/Japan. So ASQ_20, ASQ_21 and ASQ_33 are stored raw for cov_country=1 and already reverse-scored for cov_country=2 and 3; option_text_translated is therefore left blank for those three items, since no single anchor mapping is correct for the whole table. Administration: the Spanish sample read the Spanish version and the Italian and Japanese samples read separately back-translated Italian and Japanese versions (paper, Section 2.2), neither of which is published in the deposit ('Data set in Spanish'), so the shipped base wording is the administered wording for the 139 Spanish respondents only. Rights: deposit is CC BY 4.0 (figshare 13601096) and the paper is CC BY 4.0 (EJIHPE 11(1):113-128, doi 10.3390/ejihpe11010010); no fee or no-redistribution clause was found for the ASQ, so silence-is-permission applies.
public_note: Item ASQ_20, ASQ_21 and ASQ_33 responses are stored raw for the Spanish subsample (cov_country=1) but already reverse-scored for the Italian and Japanese subsamples (cov_country=2 and 3) -- the study's published subscale means only reproduce under that split (Spain F1 34.78 vs 34.74 published after reversing, Italy F1 30.22 vs 30.22 as stored) -- so no single 1-6 anchor mapping is correct for those three items and their option text is left blank; separately, the item wording shipped here is the study's Spanish version, which is what the 139 Spanish respondents read, while the 85 Italian and 130 Japanese respondents read back-translated Italian and Japanese versions that the deposit does not publish.

source_ref: BFI-44 items: https://www.ocf.berkeley.edu/~johnlab/docs.php?file=BFI-44.pdf (Berkeley Personality Lab, Measures page; PhenX DCW reproduction of John, Donahue & Kentle 1991). Response anchors + data: PLOS ONE 10.1371/journal.pone.0129015.s001 (SPSS .sav) value labels for B51..B544. Paper: Ibrahim N, Teo SSL, Che Din N, Abdul Gafor AH, Ismail R (2015) PLoS ONE 10(7):e0129015, CC BY 4.0 (Measures section states the 1-5 direction). Processing script: data/ibrahim_2015_ckd_personality_qol.py
note: Item wording is the canonical BFI-44 (John, Donahue & Kentle 1991), transcribed verbatim from BFI-44.pdf as distributed by the rights holder's own measures page (https://www.ocf.berkeley.edu/~johnlab/docs.php?file=BFI-44.pdf, linked from measures.html as 'BFI-44 (BFI-1)'; the file is a PhenX Data Collection Worksheet reproducing the instrument, protocol source phenxtoolkit.org/protocols/view/121101). The study's own source file (PLOS S1, 10.1371/journal.pone.0129015.s001) carries NO variable labels on B51..B544 -- checked at both levels, only value labels are present -- so item text could not come from the deposit and mapping_basis is reconstructed, not data_labels. Code derivation is pattern 1 (the IRW item code IS the source column name: data/ibrahim_2015_ckd_personality_qol.py melts BFI_COLS = [f'B5{i}' for i in 1..44] with no rename), so nothing positional is at risk; what is inferred is that B5<i> is BFI item <i> in canonical numbering. Verified PARTIAL, see verify_ibrahim_2015_bfi.R: the .sav's own reverse-scored duplicate columns exist for exactly {2,6,8,9,12,18,21,23,24,27,31,34,35,37,41,43} = the canonical BFI-44 reverse set (1 of choose(44,16)=2.1e11 subsets), and all five of the authors' domain sum columns (B5_Extraversion/_Agree/_Conscience/_Neuro/_Open) are reproduced exactly for all 200 respondents from the canonical key. That pins every item's domain and polarity but not its position within a domain-by-polarity class. STORED DIRECTION: raw -- B5<i>_R == 6 - B5<i> exactly, and the IRW script melts the un-reversed columns, so anchors run in the SAME direction for all 44 items (unlike conner_2017_bfi). option_text is the .sav's own value labels verbatim, lowercase as stored ('disagree strongly' .. 'agree strongly'), which are also the mapping used by MAP_BFI in the processing script and match the paper's stated 1=disagree strongly / 5=agree strongly. DEVIATIONS: (a) instructions holds only the BFI's item stem 'I see myself as someone who...'; the PDF's surrounding paragraph is the PhenX worksheet's own write-in-a-number instruction whose anchor labels ('Neither disagree nor agree') differ from the ones this study administered, so it was deliberately not shipped -- neither the paper nor the .sav records the administered instructions. (b) LANGUAGE: the paper says patients 'able to understand Malay or English language were approached' and cites a Malaysian BFI validation, but never states which language version was administered; the deposit contains no Malay wording (the .sav's only text is its English value labels). Because the administration language is not established as non-English, `language` and the _translated columns are omitted rather than asserting Malay; recorded here and in the public_note so a later pass can find it. RIGHTS: the wording was copied from the rights holder's own BFI-44 distribution, which states no terms at all -- no fee, no non-commercial clause, no redistribution bar in the PDF or on measures.html. The non-commercial sentences on ocf.berkeley.edu/~johnlab/bfi.html ('Christopher J. Soto and I hold the copyright to the BFI-2 ... At this time, the BFI-2 is for non-commercial uses only') are scoped explicitly and solely to the BFI-2, a different instrument with different copyright holders, and there is no BFI-1/BFI-44 terms page. Silence is permission, so this ships; consistent with conner_2017_bfi and CV_OASIS_ODSIS_PPE_Novak_2020_BFI (both 2026-09-04).
public_note: Item text for this table is the canonical English BFI-44 wording, taken from the Berkeley Personality Lab's own BFI-44 distribution. The study was run in a Malaysian nephrology clinic and approached patients who understood 'Malay or English'; it never states which language version of the BFI was administered, and neither the paper nor the SPSS deposit contains any Malay item wording, so for some respondents the shipped English may not be the wording they read. Responses are stored raw: resp 1 = 'disagree strongly' and 5 = 'agree strongly' for all 44 items, including the 16 canonically reverse-keyed ones.

source_ref: RAND 36-Item Health Survey 1.0 Questionnaire Items, https://www.rand.org/health-care/surveys_tools/mos/36-item-short-form/survey-instrument.html and Terms and Conditions, https://www.rand.org/health-care/surveys_tools/mos/36-item-short-form/terms.html (both fetched 2026-09-07); response categories from Ibrahim et al. (2015) PLOS ONE 10.1371/journal.pone.0129015 S1 Information (.sav) value labels
note: Item stems, instructions and section prompts are verbatim from RAND's own publication of the instrument (RAND 36-Item Health Survey 1.0 Questionnaire Items, rand.org, fetched 2026-09-07); the response options are NOT canonical -- they are the study's own SPSS value labels, verbatim, because those are the categories the live resp integers were actually derived from and they differ from the canonical wording in two visible ways: item 1's lowest category reads 'not good' where RAND prints 'Poor', and block 11 was administered on 4 categories (definitely false / mostly false / mostly true / definitely true) rather than RAND's 5, which include 'Don't know'. Verbatim also means the file's own inconsistent casing ('Yes' / 'no') is preserved. RIGHTS: the SF-36 has two rights positions and the wording shipped here was copied from the permissive one, so the SWLS rule (the licence of the source actually copied from governs) applies. RAND: 'All RAND Health-developed surveys are public documents. RAND does not charge or require permission to use.' and, in its Terms and Conditions, 'RAND hereby grants permission to use RAND 36-Item Short Form Health Survey ... No further written permission is needed for use of this Health Survey', subject to a credit line 'when printing and distributing this document acknowledging that it was developed at RAND as part of the Medical Outcomes Study' -- carried here in the instrument field. The trademarked SF-36 (Optum / QualityMetric / John Ware Research Group) is the other position, and it was checked: jwrginc.com/permission-request asks scholars to request permission and states 'You will be emailed a response to grant you royalty-free permission to utilize these surveys', i.e. no fee for research and no quotable no-redistribution clause, so neither of the two blocking triggers fires. MAPPING: the IRW item codes ARE the .sav column names (data/ibrahim_2015_ckd_personality_qol.py melts an explicit named-column list), but the .sav carries NO variable labels, so the code-to-wording tie rests on the SF-36's own question numbering (SF36Q9d = question 9d) rather than on any label -- hence reconstructed, not data_labels. resp integers are the processing script's own label-to-number map, which is REVERSED relative to the .sav's numeric codes for most blocks; verify_ibrahim_2015_sf36.R reconciles all 145 item x option cells against the raw file. SF36Q10 has no resp 4: its 5-category scale skips 'a good bit of the time', which the script's shared Q9/Q10 map assigns to 4, and the script's one kept unlabelled raw 6.0 lands at resp 6 ('all the time').
public_note: Patients completed the questionnaires in Malay or English, but only an English version of the SF-36 wording is recoverable from the deposit, so the item text shipped here is the English (RAND) wording for a partly Malay-language administration; the response options are the study's own recorded categories, which differ from the published instrument in two places -- item 1's lowest category reads 'not good' rather than 'Poor', and question 11 was administered on four categories rather than the instrument's five (there is no 'Don't know').
